title: Elasticity from a demand schedule: price elasticity, the total revenue test and substitutes
scenario: Ridgeway Pottery, an invented studio, sells handmade mugs. The table shows the number of mugs buyers demand per month at four prices.

table.caption: Mugs demanded per month at each price (invented data for practice)

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate the price elasticity of demand when the price falls from \$10 to \$8, using the starting values. Show your work.

rubric.point: Correct percent changes: quantity +50% ((150 − 100) ÷ 100) and price −20% ((8 − 10) ÷ 10)

parts.sample: Percent change in quantity: $\frac{150 - 100}{100} \times 100 = 50\%$. Percent change in price: $\frac{8 - 10}{10} \times 100 = -20\%$. Elasticity: $|50 \div (-20)| = 2.5$.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify what happens to Ridgeway's total revenue when the price falls from \$10 to \$8, and state whether this is consistent with your answer to part A.

rubric.point: Total revenue increases, from \$1,000 to \$1,200, consistent with elastic demand (elasticity above 1) in this range
accept: rises, as expected with elastic demand

parts.sample: Total revenue increases from $10 \times 100 = \$1{,}000$ to $8 \times 150 = \$1{,}200$. This is consistent with part A: an elasticity of 2.5 is greater than 1, so demand is elastic, and with elastic demand price and total revenue move in opposite directions.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Ridgeway considers cutting the price from \$6 to \$4. Using the total revenue test, explain whether demand is elastic or inelastic in this range.

rubric.point: Inelastic, because total revenue falls (\$1,080 to \$800) when the price falls: price and total revenue move in the same direction
accept: inelastic since TR falls with the price cut

parts.sample: Total revenue falls from $6 \times 180 = \$1{,}080$ to $4 \times 200 = \$800$. Price and total revenue move in the same direction, so demand is inelastic in this range.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: A new studio opens in the same town and sells handmade mugs much like Ridgeway's. Explain how this is likely to affect the price elasticity of demand for Ridgeway's mugs.

rubric.point: Demand becomes more elastic, because buyers now have a close substitute and can switch to it when Ridgeway raises its price

parts.sample: Demand for Ridgeway's mugs becomes more elastic. The new studio's mugs are a close substitute, so if Ridgeway raises its price, more buyers switch to the other studio, and quantity demanded falls by a larger percentage than before.
